Highlights ▪ Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) delivered for North Stanmore, establishing a ~20- year heavy rare earth development case with a post-tax NPV8 of A$1.21 billion, post-tax IRR of 240% and initial capital of A$155 million (including 30% contingency). ▪ Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5 years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion. ▪ Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO, underpinning 100% of the PFS production target. ▪ Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024 ppm TREO. ▪ Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006 hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore. ▪ Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent qualification. ▪ TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91% of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate. ▪ Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further high-grade material to the PFS mine plan. ▪ Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter. ASX ANNOUNCEMENT 30 October 2026


         Quarterly Activities Report – 30 September 2026

         Victory Metals (ASX:VTM) (Victory or the Company) is pleased to report on its
           activities and the Appendix 5B for the quarter ending 30 September 2026 (Quarter,
        Reporting Period).


         Highlights

           ▪   Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) delivered for North Stanmore, establishing a ~20-
            year heavy rare earth development case with a post-tax NPV8 of A$1.21 billion,
             post-tax IRR of 240% and  initial capital of A$155 million (including 30%
             contingency).
           ▪  Pre-tax NPV8 of A$1.76 billion and pre-tax IRR of 338%, with payback of ~1.5
            years from first production and life-of-mine FOB revenue of A$6.5 billion.
           ▪  Maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and 248 ppm HREO,
            underpinning 100% of the PFS production target.
           ▪  Updated Mineral Resource Estimate of 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO, including a
          maiden 70.7 Mt Measured category and a 53.3 Mt high-grade domain at 1,024
         ppm TREO.
           ▪  Mining Lease M20/564 granted on 11 September 2026, covering almost 2,006
            hectares and securing mining tenure for North Stanmore.
           ▪  Heavy rare earth concentrate dispatched from the Perth pilot plant to
             potential offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for
           independent qualification.
           ▪  TIMA mineralogy confirmed 86% of Dy, 82% of Tb, 96% of Y, 88% of Pr and 91%
             of Nd report to secondary phosphate groups in pilot plant concentrate.
           ▪  Material previously logged as saprock reclassified as saprolite, adding further
            high-grade material to the PFS mine plan.
           ▪  Company had available cash of approximately $9.18M at the end of the Quarter.



        PFS, Maiden Ore Reserve and Updated Mineral Resource Establish 20-Year
       Development Case

      On 18 August 2026, Victory released the results of the North Stanmore Pre-
          Feasibility Study (PFS), a maiden Ore Reserve and an updated Mineral Resource
        Estimate (MRE) for its 100%-owned North Stanmore Heavy Rare Earth Project near
        Cue, Western Australia.

        The PFS outlines a simple development concept: shallow, predominantly free-dig
         open-pit mining and flotation beneficiation at 2.4 Mtpa to produce ~29,000 wet
        tonnes a year of heavy rare earth-enriched mineral concentrate for sale to third-

party refiners. The schedule comprises ~10 years of mining and processing,
followed by ~10.5 years of processing stockpiled ore.

The PFS production target is underpinned entirely by the Probable Ore Reserve
and excludes Inferred Mineral Resources and Exploration Targets. Pricing adopts
long-term net payability prices deliberately discounted to current spot, with 65%
payability applied to rare earth oxides and 50% to hafnium oxide. Mincore
managed the PFS and prepared the capital estimate; MEC Mining supported mine
planning and mining cost estimation.

Maiden Ore Reserve
The PFS supports a maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 47.0 Mt at 692 ppm TREO and
248 ppm HREO (≥300 ppm TREO cut-off), containing 32.6 kt TREO and 11.6 kt HREO.

Updated Mineral Resource Estimate
The updated MRE totals 278.8 Mt at 483 ppm TREO and introduces a maiden 70.7
Mt Measured category, with Measured and Indicated Resources totalling 154.8 Mt.
The high-grade domain of 53.3 Mt at 1,024 ppm TREO retained ~97% of its August
2025 tonnage and ~99% of its grade, while Measured and Indicated high-grade
tonnage increased 7.2% to 38.0 Mt. The update incorporated 83 drill holes for 4,378
m, including 20 twin holes that confirmed existing results.

As reported on 9 July 2026, review of geological data during pilot plant operations
identified that a substantial volume of material logged as saprock is saprolite – the
ore type on which all metallurgical test work has been based. This material was
incorporated into the PFS mine plan, and PFS completion was moved to August
2026 to capture it.

Next steps
Definitive  Feasibility  Study  (DFS)  work  will  focus on  geotechnical  and
hydrogeological investigations, engineering definition, continued pilot and locked-
cycle metallurgical test work, product qualification, approvals, offtake discussions
and the funding strategy. Funding options under review include the non-binding

US EXIM Letter of Interest for up to US$190 million, project debt, strategic equity,
offtake-linked funding and government support.

Mining Lease M20/564 Granted for North Stanmore

Mining Lease M20/564, covering almost 2,006 hectares, was granted by the
Western Australian Department of Mines, Petroleum and Exploration on  11
September 2026. The grant secures mining tenure over the lease area and clears a
key hurdle on North Stanmore's development pathway.

The lease is a full conversion of P20/2248, P20/2249, P20/2250, P20/2352, P20/2409
and P20/2410, and a partial conversion of P20/2403, P20/2468, P20/2469 and
E20/871. Victory's footprint in the area is unchanged.

The grant follows the Native Title Mining Agreement executed with the Wajarri
Yamaji Aboriginal Corporation in June 2026, which supported the native title
process.  It builds on the PFS, maiden Ore Reserve and updated MRE, and
strengthens the Company's position in offtake, strategic investment and project
financing discussions.

CEO and Executive Director Brendan Clark said: "The grant of our 2,006-hectare
Mining Lease is a major milestone for Victory and an important step towards
bringing North Stanmore into production."

Heavy Rare Earth Rich Concentrate Dispatched to Potential Offtake Partners

Victory's Perth flotation pilot plant continued to operate under continuous, steady-
state conditions at ambient temperature during the Quarter, producing heavy rare
earth-enriched concentrate consistent with the 7.1% TREO result reported on 17
June 2026.

On 9 July 2026, the Company commenced dispatching concentrate to potential
offtake partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for independent
examination, analysis and qualification. This allows prospective customers to verify
the concentrate's grade, heavy rare earth distribution and low impurity profile in
their own facilities, and is a customary step in qualifying new supply sources.

The PFS confirmed that Victory is advancing confidential discussions with strategic
partners across Japan, Europe and the United States on product qualification,
pricing, commercial structures and long-term offtake.





                                                                                      Page 4 of 11

CEO and Executive Director Brendan Clark said: "Dispatching our heavy rare earth
concentrate to these partners in Australia, Japan and the United States for their
own independent examination is a significant commercial step."

TIMA Mineralogy Confirms Heavy and Magnet Rare Earths Hosted in Secondary
Phosphates

On 30 July 2026 (re-released on 4 August 2026 to include JORC Code Table 1
information),  Victory reported TESCAN  Integrated  Mineral  Analyser (TIMA)
characterisation of pilot plant concentrate, completed by ALS Metallurgy in
Balcatta, Western Australia. The concentrate was produced from a composite of 33
air core samples from 18 drill holes within Indicated Mineral Resource areas, with
an average grade of 1,189 ppm TREO and an HREO/TREO ratio of 37.5%.

TIMA classified 5.93 mass% of the concentrate as secondary rare earth phosphate
groups (2.11% churchite and similar, 3.82% rhabdophane and similar), compared
with only 1.13 mass% for the primary monazite and xenotime groups combined.
Most of the target rare earth value reports to the secondary phosphate system:

                                Deportment to secondary
         Element                                               Largest individual host
                                  phosphate groups (%)

          Dysprosium (Dy)                    86                  Churchite and similar

          Terbium (Tb)                       82                  Churchite and similar

           Yttrium (Y)                         96                              –

         Praseodymium (Pr)                 88             Rhabdophane and similar

        Neodymium (Nd)                         91              Rhabdophane and similar

      Table 2. Indicative deportment to combined churchite, rhabdophane and interphase groups.

Unlike primary monazite and xenotime, which generally require a mineral cracking
step before  leaching, North Stanmore's  rare earth value  is predominantly
associated  with  hydrated  secondary  phosphates formed  through  natural
weathering.  This supports the Company's wet screening and  flotation-led
beneficiation route ahead of selective hydrometallurgical treatment. Calcium is
predominantly hosted in feldspar rather than reactive carbonates, which  is
favourable for acid consumption.

The deportment results are indicative. ALS noted a high degree of uncertainty for
Pr and Nd and a very high degree of uncertainty for Tb and Dy, and recommended
LA-ICP-MS analysis to refine phase compositions. The TIMA study does not by itself
establish leach recovery, reagent consumption or final process conditions.
